summary.intent: Run the GSD plan-phase workflow to produce executable PLAN.md files for roadmap phase 68.2 (SDK-owned read chain and resolved folder listings), then execute those plans wave-by-wave via the execute-phase workflow, while also spinning up an independent git worktree to parallelize planning/execution of phase 69.
summary.outcome: Phase 68.2 planning completed end-to-end (research, Nyquist VALIDATION.md, D-07 scope decision locked, pattern mapping, 4 requirements registered, 12 plans across 7 waves, plan-checker PASSED with 2 non-blocking warnings, coverage gates 13/13) and committed across 7 commits; execution began sequentially on the main tree with Waves 1 and 2 completed and independently verified (ROT-07 gate holds, 296-300 tests passing), Wave 3 in progress; a separate worktree for phase 69 was created off origin/main at cipher-box-phase69 ready for the user to kick off in a new session.

repo: plan:pre hook activation for the UI capability is gated by a `when` condition classifying the phase type (net-new UI surface vs architecture/refactor); a lower-level ui-plan-gate check can report block:true even when the higher-level hook never activates, so §5.6 must check activeHooks, not just the raw check result.

The `gsd-tools query commit` helper has a known false-negative: it can report `commit_failed` even though the commit landed cleanly in git log — always verify via `git log` rather than trusting the reported status.

New phase_req_ids marked 'new' in ROADMAP must be registered in REQUIREMENTS.md (requirement section, traceability rows, coverage summary) before the planner runs so coverage gates have a stable target.

Worktree parallel execution depends on `worktree.baseRef` config: if it defaults to 'fresh' (off origin/main) instead of 'head', executor worktrees would fork without the branch's PLAN.md commits — this must be explicitly verified before dispatching, not assumed.

In this pnpm monorepo, worktree-based parallel executors each need their own `pnpm install` (expensive); for phases where most waves are single-plan, running sequentially on the main tree reuses installed node_modules and is more robust than orchestrating worktree create/merge/cleanup per wave.
The advisory gap-analysis check's parser chokes on control characters in the `rendered` field output; running the underlying check directly is a viable workaround.
The schema-gate planner contribution is orchestrator-evaluated (not always injected) — skip injecting it when the phase touches no ORM/DB schema files.
Intel API-surface extraction (§7.9) can return 0 symbols for this monorepo; when empty it's HINT-only and should be omitted from the planner prompt rather than passed as noise.

code.finding: resolveChildren docstring documents that per-child skip-on-resolve/unseal-failure is security-sound because the parent folder is already gated via Plan-01's ensureFolderLoaded/dfsFindFolder before this runs — an unverifiable sibling is simply omitted (availability tradeoff), never rendered with stale/attacker content, and navigating into any child re-triggers the ROT-07 gate.

enforceResolved also wired into dfsFindFolder's child loop; pre-existing write-path gate remains at line 1156 for comparison.

workflow: Independently spot-check and re-run acceptance/security tests after each executor completes rather than trusting the subagent's self-reported PLAN COMPLETE summary, especially for security-critical or deviation-flagged changes.

When a user wants parallel independent work in a separate worktree while the current session keeps driving other work, use plain `git worktree add` rather than an EnterWorktree-style tool that would switch the current session's context.
Reserve AskUserQuestion for genuine decision gates (research-first vs skip-research, ambiguous scope boundaries like D-07, auto-advance vs manual review) rather than asking for routine steps.
For monorepos where most waves in a phase are single-plan, sequential execution on the main tree can be both simpler and more correct than parallel worktree execution.
